name: Luleå
title: Thickness Gauging at Luleå | Ice-Class Bulk Carriers & Ore
description: Thickness gauging at Luleå for ice-class bulk carriers in the ore and steel trades: cargo holds, ice belt, ballast tanks and bow structure, in and out of ice.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ore Carriers and Ice-Class Ships at the Port of Luleå
intro: Luleå, near the head of the Bothnian Bay, is the largest port in Sweden's far north and the sea outlet for Norrbotten's ore and steel industry. Ice-class bulk carriers load iron ore pellets and bring in coal and other raw materials for the steelworks, working through a winter in which the bay freezes and icebreakers escort ships in and out. Hull and hold gauging here is planned around that ice season. For every job the technicians travel from India and join the ship in port.

highlights.h: Ice belts after a Bothnian Bay winter
highlights.p: The Bothnian Bay has the longest and hardest ice season in the Baltic. Ships trading to Luleå through winter come out of it with abraded ice belts, dented bow plating and sometimes cracked frames, which spring gauging and crack detection put on record.

highlights.h: Ore pellet holds and wing tanks
highlights.p: Iron ore pellets are dense and abrasive, and loading them concentrates weight on tank tops and hopper plating. Hold gauging at the ore quay, with readings in the hopper and topside tanks, gives owners a working picture of wastage between surveys.

The Malmporten project will dredge the fairway between 2027 and 2030 and add a new deep-water port, so that larger bulk carriers can call. Owners planning tonnage for that trade will want condition data on the ships they intend to deploy.

port.h: Luleå: the Bothnian Bay's ore and steel port
p: Luleå occupies a peninsula at the mouth of the Lule River in the north-western corner of the Bothnian Bay, the northernmost basin of the Baltic. The city and port are surrounded by an archipelago of hundreds of islands, and ships reach the harbour along a long piloted fairway from open water. There is no tide to speak of, and the bay's water is only slightly brackish. What sets Luleå apart is ice: the bay freezes every winter, fast ice forms in the archipelago and drift ice covers the open water, and the port is kept open by icebreakers that escort ships through the channel. Luleå is also the home port of the Swedish state icebreaker fleet, which spends its summers here between seasons.

Cargo is dominated by the region's heavy industry. Iron ore pellets from LKAB's mines in the interior arrive by rail and are loaded onto bulk carriers, while the SSAB steelworks beside the harbour receives coal, coke and other raw materials, and steel and other products also move through the port. Oil products, forest products and general cargo make up the balance. The trade is about to change in scale: under the Malmporten project, run by the Swedish Maritime Administration and the Port of Luleå, about forty kilometres of fairway are to be dredged between 2027 and 2030, with a new deep-water port and land areas, and the deeper channel is being paired with a new, larger icebreaker. Until then, the size of ship that can call is set by the present fairway depth.

For gauging, the calendar matters more than at almost any other European port. Ships that trade here in winter need high ice class and the hull to match it, and the season leaves its mark on the ice belt, bow and frames. Most owners schedule dockings and large gauging programmes for the open-water months, while winter calls are used for work inside holds, tanks and machinery spaces. Ore carriers load quickly once the shiploader starts, so the window for hold work is the time between arrival and the start of loading. Ships discharging coal or other bulk for the steelworks stay longer, and their holds become available one at a time as discharge proceeds. Either way, the scope has to be agreed before arrival, because there is little slack in an ore port's schedule.

facilities.h: Gauging at Luleå's ore, bulk and general cargo berths
p: On an ore carrier, the holds are empty on arrival and filled rapidly once loading begins, so the gauging scope is planned for the hours or days before the shiploader reaches each hold. Tank tops, hopper plating, frames and brackets are measured and any damage from previous cargoes recorded, and hopper and topside tanks can be entered once the crew has issued gas-free certificates and entry permits. At the discharge berths serving the steelworks the sequence runs the other way, with holds coming free as the cargo comes out. General cargo and oil berths offer the usual afloat scopes on ballast tanks, deck structure and voids.

Luleå has no drydock for ships of this kind, so dockings take place at yards in Finland, elsewhere in the Baltic or further away, usually in summer. That makes the spring and early summer calls at Luleå valuable for pre-docking gauging: the shell is free of ice, the winter's damage is visible, and readings taken then let the yard and the class surveyor prepare the steel list and close-up survey plan before the ship arrives. In mid-winter, external work on the shell and open decks is limited by intense cold and very short days, although work inside the hull continues.
list: Ore loading berths — hold, hopper and topside tank gauging on bulk carriers before loading starts, with earlier damage recorded.
Discharge berths for the steelworks — hold readings on coal and raw-material carriers as each hold empties.
General cargo and oil berths — ballast tank, void and deck measurements on short-sea ships and tankers.
Spring calls in open water — ice-belt, bow and forefoot gauging and crack detection before the summer docking.
Docking yards in Finland and around the Baltic — completion of renewal survey programmes in the yard period.

context.h: Ice-class rules, regulation and industrial change at Luleå
p: Ships at Luleå are inspected under the Paris MoU by the Swedish Transport Agency. Every winter the Swedish Maritime Administration announces traffic restrictions for the Bothnian Bay, and Luleå is among the first ports to come under them and the last to be released: only ships with the required Finnish-Swedish ice class and size are given icebreaker escort. Ice class is therefore a condition of trading here in winter, not an optional notation. Wasted ice-belt plating or frames that have lost section reduce the margin the strengthening was designed to give, and a ship that comes out of a Bothnian Bay winter with damage needs it measured and assessed before it goes back into the ice.

The industry around Luleå is investing heavily in fossil-free iron and steel, with new processes planned at the mines and the steelworks, and Malmporten is designed to give that industry deeper-draught ships and more capacity by the winter of 2030–31. For shipowners, the shift will bring different cargoes and larger ships into a trade that has long relied on ice-classed bulk carriers of moderate size. Owners and charterers considering tonnage for Luleå, or extending the life of ships already in the trade, will want a clear picture of hull, hold and ice-belt condition, and thickness measurement on the current fleet is where that picture starts.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs we see at Luleå
jobs.p: Luleå work follows the ice. In spring and early summer, owners of ice-class bulk carriers ask for the winter's damage to be measured before the docking; during the open-water season, hold and tank scopes are added to loading and discharge calls; in winter, the work stays inside the hull. Ore carriers bring tight windows before loading begins, while ships discharging for the steelworks give more time. Many of these jobs feed a renewal survey or docking at a Baltic yard, where our readings from Luleå become part of a single report. For ships that return to Luleå regularly, ice-season and summer readings can be compared year on year.
list: Spring ice-belt and bow gauging with MPI at frame connections on an ice-class bulk carrier after a winter of ore voyages.
Hold, hopper and topside tank gauging on an ore carrier before loading, ahead of an intermediate survey.
Ballast tank and double-bottom readings on a bulk carrier discharging coal for the steelworks, as a pre-docking steel estimate.
Hatch coaming and deck crack checks on an ice-class bulker after heavy ice transits.
On-hire condition gauging on a bulk carrier chartered into the Bothnian Bay ore trade.

logistics: The team flies via Stockholm Arlanda to Luleå Airport, a short road journey from the port. Technicians come from India on Schengen visas, which also cover onward travel to docking yards in Finland or elsewhere in the Schengen area. Port access is controlled, and the ship's agent arranges entry to the ore, steelworks and cargo berths, including any site inductions. Winter jobs need cold-weather equipment and extra margin in the schedule, because ice delays arrivals and daylight is very short.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged at Luleå during the ice season?
faqs.a: Yes, inside the hull. Holds, ballast tanks, machinery spaces and piping can be measured whenever the ship is alongside and the spaces are prepared. External shell and open-deck work is slowed by severe cold and darkness in mid-winter, so ice-belt readings are best taken in spring, when the shell is clear and the damage is visible.

faqs.q: When should an ore carrier's holds be gauged at Luleå?
faqs.a: Before loading reaches them. Ore pellets go in quickly once the shiploader starts, and a loaded hold cannot be measured, so we plan with the chief officer to gauge each hold in the time between arrival and the start of loading in that hold. If the stay is short, the scope is prioritised so the most important frames and plates are measured first.

faqs.q: Does icebreaker escort mean the hull still needs checking after winter?
faqs.a: It does. Escort reduces the risk of a ship getting stuck, but the ship still breaks and pushes through ice in the channel and in the broken track behind the icebreaker, and ridged or compressed ice still loads the bow and sides. Abrasion, indents and cracked frames are common after a hard season, so spring gauging and crack detection remain worthwhile.

faqs.q: Where do ships trading to Luleå go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: To yards in Finland, elsewhere in the Baltic or further afield, chosen by the owner and usually timed for summer. Readings taken at Luleå are tied to the TM plan's frame and strake references, so the yard and the class surveyor can use them, and our team can travel on to complete the programme at the docking yard.
